title: ECOSolveR Examples
text: solve following problem arises example sparse signal reconstruction problems compressed sensing:  \begin{array}{ll} \text{minimize}   & \|x\|_1 \\ \text{subject } & Ax = b \end{array} \qquad (L_1) x\R^n, \R^{m \times n} m\leq n. Reformulate problem expressing L_1 norm x follows  \begin{aligned} x &\leq u \\ -x &\leq u \end{aligned} u\R^n minimize sum u. reformulated problem using stacked variables z = \begin{pmatrix}x\\u\end{pmatrix} now  \begin{array}{ll} \text{minimize}   & c^{\top}z \\ \text{subject } & \tilde{}z = b \\                   & Gz \leq h \end{array} \qquad \text{(LP)}  inequality respective positive orthant. R code generates random instance problem solves . First, function generate random sparse matrices normal entries. Note ECOS expects sparse matrices, ordinary matrices. check solution found. Extract solution.
code: library(ECOSolveR) library(Matrix) set.seed(182391) n <- 1000L m <- 10L density <- 0.01 c <- c(rep(0.0, n), rep(1.0, n)) sprandn <- function(nrow, ncol, density) {     items <- ceiling(nrow * ncol * density)     matrix(c(rnorm(items),              rep(0, nrow * ncol - items)),            nrow = nrow) } A <- sprandn(m, n, density) Atilde <- Matrix(cbind(A, matrix(rep(0.0, m * n), nrow = m)), sparse = TRUE) b <- rnorm(m) I <- diag(n) G <- rbind(cbind(I, -I),            cbind(-I, -I)) G <- as(G, "dgCMatrix") h <- rep(0.0, 2L * n) dims <- list(l = 2L * n, q = NULL, e = 0L) ## Solve the problem z <- ECOS_csolve(c = c, G = G, h = h, dims = dims, A = Atilde, b = b) names(z) ## [1] "x"          "y"          "s"          "z"          "infostring" ## [6] "retcodes"   "summary"    "timing" z$infostring ## [1] "Optimal solution found" x <- z$x[1:n] u <- z$x[(n+1):(2*n)] nnzx = sum(abs(x) > 1e-8) sprintf("x reconstructed with %d non-zero entries", nnzx / length(x) * 100) ## [1] "x reconstructed with 1 non-zero entries"

what: Parametric Optimization with the Update-Solve Loop
title: ECOSolveR Examples
text: solving sequence related problems share sparsity structure differ numerical data, multi-step lifecycle API avoids repeating expensive symbolic analysis KKT ordering phase. pattern : ECOS_setup() — one-time setup (symbolic analysis) Loop: ECOS_update() + ECOS_solve() — cheap re-solves ECOS_cleanup() — free workspace vary right-hand side h LP previous example, tracing optimal value changes scale h. comparison, sweep using ECOS_csolve() loop call ECOS_setup ECOS_cleanup every iteration. lifecycle API particularly beneficial problem dimensions large setup dominates solve time.
code: ## Set up workspace once ws <- ECOS_setup(c = c, G = G, h = h, dims = dims, A = Atilde, b = b)  ## Sweep a parameter: scale h from 0 to 1 alphas <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 11) pcosts <- numeric(length(alphas))  for (i in seq_along(alphas)) {     ECOS_update(ws, h = h + alphas[i])     res <- ECOS_solve(ws)     pcosts[i] <- res$summary[["pcost"]] }  ECOS_cleanup(ws)  ## Show results data.frame(alpha = alphas, pcost = round(pcosts, 4)) ##    alpha     pcost ## 1    0.0   12.8872 ## 2    0.1  -87.1128 ## 3    0.2 -187.1128 ## 4    0.3 -287.1128 ## 5    0.4 -387.1128 ## 6    0.5 -487.1128 ## 7    0.6 -587.1128 ## 8    0.7 -687.1128 ## 9    0.8 -787.1128 ## 10   0.9 -887.1128 ## 11   1.0 -987.1128

title: Embedded Conic Solver in R
text: Embedded Conic Solver R. R wrapper around ecos project GitHub describes ECOS . ECOS numerical software solving convex second-order cone programs (SOCPs) type \text{Minimize } \mathbf{c}^\top\mathbf{x} \text{ } \mathbf{}\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b} \text{ } \mathbf{G}\mathbf{x} \leq_{\mathbf{K}} \mathbf{h} last inequality generalized, , \mathbf{h} - \mathbf{G}\mathbf{x} belongs cone \mathbf{K}. ECOS supports positive orthant \mathbf{R}_+, second-order cones \mathbf{Q}_n defined \mathbf{Q}_n = \bigl\lbrace (t, \mathbf{x}) \mid t \geq \lVert \mathbf{x} \rVert_2 \bigr\rbrace t scalar \mathbf{x} \\mathbf{R}^{n-1}, exponential cone \mathbf{K}_e defined \mathbf{K}_e = \text{closure} \bigl\lbrace (x, y, z) \mid \exp(x/z) \leq y/z,\ z > 0 \bigr\rbrace, (x, y, z) \\mathbf{R}^3. cone \mathbf{K} therefore direct product positive orthant, second-order, exponential cones: \mathbf{K} = \mathbf{R}_+ \times \mathbf{Q}_{n_1} \times \cdots \times \mathbf{Q}_{n_N} \times \mathbf{K}_e \times \cdots \times \mathbf{K}_e.

title: ECOSolveR 0.6.1
text: CRAN release: 2026-02-18 Fix UBSan error (misaligned pointer REAL() zero-length vector) build_result() equality constraints present (p = 0). Reported CRAN M1 SAN checks. Add multi-step solver lifecycle API: ECOS_setup(), ECOS_solve(), ECOS_update(), ECOS_cleanup() allow re-solving problems changed numerical data (sparsity structure) without repeating symbolic analysis. Workspace held external pointer GC finalizer; user data vectors duplicated prevent corruption ECOS -place equilibration. Switch R-level error messaging stop() cli::cli_abort() inline markup ({.arg}, {.cls}, {.code}, {.field}). cli package now Imports. Add lifecycle tests (10 tests covering setup, solve, update, cleanup, helper functions).

title: ECOSolveR 0.5-7
text: Switch ECOS submodule fork (bnaras/ecos, r-patches branch); remove ecos-2954b2a-changes/ overlay simplify Makevars. Fix copy-paste bug matrix validation (inherits(G,...) used instead inherits(,...)). Enable dimension consistency check (sum(q) + l + 3*e == nrow(G)). Signal R error instead returning silent NULL ECOS_setup ECOS_BB_setup fails. Fix R_init function name match package name (R_init_ECOSolveR). Narrow import(methods) importFrom(methods, ). C solver fixes: wright omega Taylor series bug, NULL dereference memory leaks ECOS_BB, integer truncation pfloat rounding, missing include guards, printf replaced Rprintf. Cherry-pick upstream NaN bail-(PR #181) ECOS_updateData NULL-safety fix (PR #185) ECOS develop branch. Add unit tests ecos.control, make_csc_matrix, dimension validation, plain-matrix handling. Fix test-bb.R namespace-qualify Matrix::sparseMatrix.
